## 5. INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE and UX

### 5.1 Marketing site (public, SEO)
URL tree (all under existing `/game-servers/directory`, minecraft stays `/servers`, link the two):
```
/game-servers/directory                      HUB
/game-servers/directory/<game>               GAME page
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<country>     COUNTRY page   (e.g. /rust/germany)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<mode>        MODE page      (e.g. /rust/pvp-vanilla, /minecraft/skyblock)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/best          "Best <game> servers" curated (monthly refresh, human-reviewed intro)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<country>/<mode>  only if >= thresholds (rare)
/game-servers/directory/s/<slug>             SERVER page  (ONLY Nxeon-hosted or owner-claimed+verified+described)
/directory/remove  /directory/add  /directory/probe-info   utility pages (noindex except probe-info)
```
Wireframes:
- **Hub**: hero ("Find a public server for <N> games" with live total only when real), search box (game or server name), game cover grid sorted by live players (cover tile = existing component), "Featured on Nxeon" shelf (<=6, rules below), region tabs, footer with Valve/other attributions and the "how listing works / remove your server" links, CTA band "Host your own - from $X/mo" and "List your server (free)".
- **Game page**: breadcrumb; H1 "<Game> public servers (live)"; stat strip (servers online, players now, countries) with "updated N min ago"; filter bar (country, mode, players band, passworded, modded, "Hosted on Nxeon"); list (20/page, server-rendered, paginated with `rel=next/prev` not infinite-scroll) rows = [cover or game glyph] name, address copy button, mode chip, country flag, players/max bar, ping-from-region, last seen; right rail: "Run a server like these" CTA tied to the game's hosting page + game's mod/pack links; below fold: 150-300 words of unique, human-written guide (how to join, popular modes, how Nxeon verifies) + FAQ. Aggregate stats per country as a small table (internal linking).
- **Country/mode page**: same template, H1 "<Mode> <Game> servers in <Country>", unique stat sentence generated from data (counts, busiest hours from our history - real), top 10, and links to sibling countries/modes.
- **Server page** (only when it passes the gate): name, owner description (moderated), join instructions per game (copy-paste), live status, 7-day uptime/peak chart (from our samples), screenshots (approved), "Hosted on Nxeon" badge + "Host your own like this" CTA, nearby/similar servers, report/claim buttons. Reason for gating: thin/duplicate content risk; individual pages for 100k stranger servers = doorway pages.
- **Indexing policy (extends INDEX_MIN_DESCRIBED)**: index only if ALL: >= 5 servers ALIVE in last 24 h (probe verified) for the page's facet; >= 3 with owner description or >= 10 with distinct non-templated names; unique intro text present; data fresh (<24 h); no more than 50% of rows from one IP/ASN/hoster (anti-spam-farm). Else `noindex,follow` and omitted from the sitemap, but still crawlable by users (links keep working). Paginated pages 2+ are `noindex,follow`; canonical to page 1 (query-param filters canonicalise to the clean URL). Server pages: index only Nxeon-hosted/claimed with description >=60 chars + 7-day uptime >=80%; all others have no page (modal on list). Sitemap `lastmod` = last meaningful change, not every refresh. Nothing programmatic should create pages for combos with <thresholds (prevents the 100k thin-page trap).
- Structured data: `BreadcrumbList` everywhere; `ItemList` (+ `ListItem` name/url) on list pages; `FAQPage` only on pages with visible FAQ content; `Organization` already global. There is NO schema.org type for a game server listing: do NOT fake `Product`/`Review`/`AggregateRating`/`VideoGame` per server (policy-risky). `WebPage` + `dateModified` is fine.
- Other: `rel="ugc nofollow noopener"` on owner links (existing); Valve attribution link followed (`rel="noopener"` only) per Steam terms; no outbound links to a hoster unless owner-approved; hreflang not needed for v2.0 (English only; country pages are targeted content, not translations).
- Avoiding duplicate/thin content: unique intro per game and per big country (humans + Claude drafts, human-reviewed), real computed stats, canonical rules above, no "x servers in <city>" templated pages (country max), consistent H1/title schema ("Best Rust servers 2026 - live list | Nxeon" only when the page really is refreshed monthly; no fake year bumps).

### 5.2 Customer portal
- `/dashboard/servers/browse` (name TBD, inside the existing portal shell): tabs [Browse | Favourites | My listings]. Left filters: game (multi), country/region, mode, players (min/max or "has players", "not full"), ping-from-your-region (we know the viewer's country via geo-ip; nearest probe region), passworded, modded, "Nxeon-hosted", sort (players, recently verified, uptime, newest). Result card same as marketing row + [Favourite star] [Copy address] [Join help]. Empty-state: "No servers yet for <game>/<filter>: Host the first one".
- **CTA** "Host your own like this": on each card/row for games we host, deep-links to `/deploy?game=<family>&preset=<mode>` with the matching preset when one exists (existing preset system for free-MC; paid presets map from taxonomy); a CTA is not attributed to a competitor's server by name.
- **Opt-in listing** (existing Public Directory card in Settings + new wizard): choose server, tagline, mode chips, picture (review queue), website (approved), toggle on/off (immediate), shows preview "this is exactly what the public sees". For non-Nxeon servers: "Add a server you run elsewhere" -> S11 verify flow (any game). Free for everyone: it is the acquisition funnel for the listing owner (and a data moat for us).
- **Favourites**: sensible and cheap (`DirectoryFavourite(userId, serverKey)`; max 50); gives logged-in return visits (retention is the known weak point per memory notes: only ~5% of signups return). Notification "your favourite is online/full" later (optional, not P1).
- **Badge and featured rules** (put in code as constants, display the rule publicly): "Hosted on Nxeon" badge = server is actually on an active Nxeon plan (not just opted in via Steam row dedupe) AND not suspended; `nxeon` entries win dedupe (existing). **Featured** = admin-curated, max 6 on hub / 3 per game page, rotating, labelled "Featured" (not "Sponsored"), selection criteria published (verified-alive >= 7 days, described, approved image, no reports); NEVER purchasable (existing "nobody can buy a position" rule: keep). Ordering default stays: image, Nxeon, busiest - but add a hard cap so Nxeon rows can't exceed ~30% of the first page on a game with real external supply (otherwise the directory looks like an ad; credibility is the whole product).
- Honesty line to put in the UI: "Public servers are listed from official server lists and owner submissions and re-checked by Nxeon. Nxeon does not run or endorse them."

## 2. SOURCE MATRIX

### 2.1 Risk classes (read this first)

| Class | What it is | Examples | Default stance |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Direct protocol query | We send the game's own query packet (A2S_INFO, MC Status/SLP, RakNet unconnected ping) to an ADDRESS. The protocol is the game's public interface. No third party's database is copied. | A2S UDP, SLP TCP, Bedrock UDP 19132, Quake/Source-engine queries | GREEN, provided the address came from a permitted source and we are polite (rate, no scanning). |
| B. Official API / master server operated by the game's publisher | Valve Web API, Vintage Story master, FiveM/Cfx backend, TruckersMP API | GetServerList | AMBER: read terms; attribute; keep keys private; revocable. |
| C. Third-party aggregator API | BattleMetrics API, GameMonitoring, etc. | | RED until terms read; their business IS this list. Prefer link-out. |
| D. HTML scraping of third-party listing sites | Parsing minecraft-server-list pages, serverlist.gg, top-games.net, etc. | | RED. Almost all such sites forbid automated access in their ToS and/or robots.txt; also database-right/copyright exposure (EU sui generis, contract). NOT RECOMMENDED for any game. Never "just a few pages" at scale. |
| E. Active discovery (scanning address space) | Masscan/Shodan-style probing to find servers | | RED (abuse reports, ISP AUP, legal). Never. We only probe addresses we were given or learned from A/B sources. |
| F. Owner-submitted | A server owner submits their own address and proves control. | | GREEN (consent + verification). Our main answer for games without a list. |

Key principle: ADDRESSES and live status are the minimum data we need. Names/descriptions from strangers are untrusted text (already sanitised by `cleanText`).

### 2.2 Per-source detail

Rating key: GREEN low, AMBER read-before-launch, RED do not use. "Terms" column states what I actually read vs. UNVERIFIED.

**S1. Steam master list: `IGameServersService/GetServerList` (and the UDP master protocol)**
- Access: HTTPS with a free Steam Web API key (we do not yet hold one; the owner must register; I did not). `filter=\appid\N\dedicated\1`, `limit` (code caps at 5000). Alternative with NO key: the UDP Master Server Query Protocol at `hl2master.steampowered.com:27011` (https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Master_Server_Query_Protocol). It is throttled by Valve and paginated by IP; the Web API is easier and more reliable. The Web API terms below only cover the Web API; the UDP protocol is documented on the Valve Developer Community wiki but I found no usage terms either way (UNVERIFIED) - so do not treat it as a way around the terms.
- Data: addr (ip:queryPort), gameport, name, appid, gamedir, version, region (Steam region id), players, max_players, bots, map, secure (VAC), dedicated, os, gametype (tag string). Not given: country (we geoip), description, uptime, ping (we measure), website.
- Cadence: list is live; sweep every 30-60 min is plenty (stats age fast). Rate limit: terms say 100,000 calls/day (our need: <=11-35 games x 24-48 sweeps = <2k/day). 
- Terms: READ https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms on 2026-10-03. Clauses that matter:
  - "You may not present the Steam Data ... so that it appears (a) that your Application is endorsed or affiliated with Valve or Steam, or (b) to be available from a third party."
  - Must "implement the Valve name(s), logo(s), and links to Valve ... on any Web page incorporating the Steam Web API and/or Steam Data" per the Steam Web API documentation, and may not "tag links to Valve ... with a 'nofollow' attribute" (so the attribution link must be a plain followed link; our existing rel="ugc nofollow" rule must NOT be applied to it).
  - "You will inform the end user about any Steam Data you will store, and you will store the Steam Data in a country (or countries) identified in your privacy policy."
  - "limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day."
  - Valve "may change, suspend or discontinue the Steam Web API and suspend or terminate your use ... at any time for any reason, without notice."
  - Key must stay confidential, not shared with third parties (we only call server-side).
  - Also "You will only retrieve Steam Data about a Steam end user as requested by the end user" - applies to user profile data; server lists are not user data, but we must NEVER add any Steam-ID/player-name fetch to the directory. (A2S_PLAYER names are player data: do NOT store.)
- Caching/republishing: terms contain no explicit caching-duration limit and no explicit ban on public display of server-list data, but they are written around an "Application" and end users, so using it for a public SEO directory is an interpretation, not an explicit grant. Honest rating: **AMBER**. Mitigation = literal compliance with the three clauses above, plus our own A2S re-verification (the numbers we show are ours, taken from the server directly, with Steam only as the way we learned the address).
- Attribution text (proposal): footer on every page that shows Steam-discovered servers: "Server addresses discovered via the Steam master server list. Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks of Valve Corporation. Nxeon is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve." with a followed link to https://store.steampowered.com/ and the Valve name/logo as the docs require (owner/designer must check the exact current brand-asset rules in the Steamworks Web API docs: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi - behind a login wall for some pages, UNVERIFIED). NOTE a tension: clause (b) "available from a third party" - our UI must not say "list provided by X"; saying "discovered via Steam" is attribution, not offering it as someone else's.
- Steam trademark/IP: we also must not use Steam store art as covers without checking its licence. Current covers are the owner's own art; keep it that way.
- Families it covers (appid MUST be verified per game before enabling; ids beyond the 11 already in code are from memory and UNVERIFIED): valheim, rust, cs2, tf2, gmod, l4d2, cs16 (appid 10), projectzomboid, ark (ASE), unturned, sdtd, conan, dayz (221100), arma3 (107410), squad (393380), mordhau (629760), kf2 (232090), sandstorm (581320), barotrauma (602960), spaceengineers (244850), empyrion (383120), stationeers (544550), theforest (242760), sonsoftheforest (1326470), vrising (1604030, servers have a ListOnSteam option), abioticfactor (427410), soulmask (2646460), necesse (1169040), theisle (376210), enshrouded (1203620, UNVERIFIED that servers are on the master list). Procedure: owner-approved one-off test call per appid; if the sample returns 0 rows, the game goes to the "no public source" bucket.
- Gotchas: (1) returned `addr` port is the QUERY port; join port is `gameport` (existing parser handles). Some games (Rust) fine, Source-engine games where `gameport`=0 -> query port. (2) Very large lists (Rust, CS2, CS 1.6, GMod: likely 5-30k rows each; UNVERIFIED sizes) -> `limit` cap hides the tail; rank by players or filter `\empty\0`/`\noplayers`. (3) Honeypot/spam servers: ~10-20% of public Source lists are fake/"player count spoofed" (well known problem): our own A2S probe + a sanity rule (players <= max, reject max>128 for most games, reject names that are only URLs) removes most.

Protocol doc: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Server_List_Ping (was wiki.vg). No key, no login, no terms - the protocol is how every client lists servers. Rating: GREEN as a protocol, but ONLY for addresses given/permitted. We need a source of addresses (below).

Per secondary sources: don't use Mojang/Minecraft brand elements in a way that implies affiliation, "Minecraft" not as the first word of a name, and include a "not affiliated with Mojang AB or Microsoft" disclaimer (primary page not re-read by me: UNVERIFIED wording; the disclaimer is cheap and the existing /servers pages likely already carry something - check).

Their public "APIs" (where they exist) are generally voting-verification or owner-status APIs with a per-server key, not list exports. HTML scraping is class D = RED. I did not read any of these sites' terms (UNVERIFIED), and I recommend you do not let any agent do so by crawling. **S10. Per-game protocols for "other" Valve-like engines** (direct A2S - class A; any address we legitimately hold)
- A2S_INFO (UDP, Source query; since 2020 requires challenge handshake): name, map, folder, game, appid, players, max, bots, type, OS, visibility (password flag), VAC, version, EDF (gameport, steamid, keywords/tags, gameid). Doc: https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Server_queries. Cheap (<200 B/packet). Do NOT call A2S_PLAYER/A2S_RULES for listing (player names/rules = unnecessary data; rules can be large).
- Other direct protocols worth a prober module (all publisher/community documented, GREEN): Terraria has no query (TShock REST per server needs token; skip) - prober = TCP connect check only (weak proof; label "reachable" not "players"); Satisfactory: HTTPS API on 7777 (`/api/v1` with auth; `HealthCheck` is unauthenticated, UNVERIFIED) - use TCP/UDP reachability only; Palworld: REST API is auth-protected -> TCP/UDP reachability or in-game list only; Enshrouded: A2S on the query port (UNVERIFIED), V Rising: A2S; Factorio: RCON-free, UDP 34197 "ping" not a documented query; Core Keeper: no query (uses Game ID via Steam relay). Where a game has no usable probe the server is listed as "unverified (cannot be probed)" with a lower rank and a much shorter TTL (see 3.4), or not listed at all.

**S11. Owner-submitted + verified (new, all games) - the universal answer**
- Flow: owner (or visitor with an Nxeon account) enters game + address (+port). We issue a one-time token like `nxeon-verify-7f3a9c`. Owner puts it in the server name / MOTD / server description / `ServerDescription` / Palworld `ServerName` etc. for a few minutes. Our prober queries the server directly; if the token appears in the response (Minecraft MOTD, A2S name, Bedrock MOTD, FiveM `sv_projectName`/`sv_projectDesc` via single/<code>), the server is `verified`, the owner may remove the token. Games with no readable name field: fallback = DNS TXT record `_nxeon-verify.<domain>` (only works for domain users) or "log in as the Nxeon customer who owns that hosted server" (Nxeon-hosted path, already trusted).
- This avoids: spam, impersonation, DoS-by-listing (an attacker submitting a victim's IP to make us probe it - mitigated by verification-before-repeat-probing: only ONE probe before verify, then none unless token matches), scraping risk.
- Rating: GREEN (consent). Cost: the verification UX and abuse controls (3.6).

**S12. Nxeon-hosted (paid, free-MC, community)** - GREEN, already built. Probe via internal knowledge instead of the internet.

## 3. DATA MODEL

### 3.1 Principle
Keep the pure `DirEntry` core and dedupe unchanged (connKey/ipKey). Rename conceptually: `ExternalServer` -> directory rows from any provider. Do additive Prisma changes (the repo has no `migrations/` dir, schema is pushed: be careful, all additive/nullable, per MEMORY note on schema rollback).

### 3.2 `ExternalServer` additions (nullable or defaulted)
```
provider        String   // replaces meaning of `source`: "steam" | "owner" | "vintagestory" | "fivem" | ...  (keep `source` for back-compat; backfill provider = source)
attributionKey  String?  // "steam" -> which footer/attribution block to render
verifiedBy      String?  // null | "provider" | "probe" | "token" | "nxeon"
verifiedAt      DateTime?
claimedByUserId String?  // owner who claimed/submitted (FK User, SetNull)
claimToken      String?  // hashed; never exposed
// liveness (written by the prober, not by the ingest)
status          String   @default("UNKNOWN") // UNKNOWN | ALIVE | DEGRADED | DEAD
lastProbeAt     DateTime?
lastAliveAt     DateTime?
consecutiveFails Int     @default(0)
latencyMs       Int?     // our measured RTT from the probe node (label "ping from <region>")
probeKind       String?  // "a2s" | "slp" | "raknet" | "tcp" | "http"
uptime7d        Float?   // from DirectoryProbeSample rollups
// geo
country         String?  // ISO-2 via lib/geo-ip.ts at insert/IP change
region          String?  // continent code (EU/NA/SA/AS/OC/AF) derived from country
// taxonomy (normalised; raw source tags kept in `tags`)
mode            String?  // game-specific enum, e.g. minecraft: survival|skyblock|factions|...; rust: vanilla|modded|...
modded          Boolean?
passworded      Boolean?
os              String?
categories      String[] // our taxonomy slugs (section 3.5)
flags           Json?    // per-game extras: {"vac":true,"wipe":"weekly","crossplay":true}
// moderation
hidden          Boolean  @default(false) // exists
hiddenReason    String?  // "optout" | "spam" | "report" | "admin"
reportCount     Int      @default(0)
ownerNote       String?  // the owner's description (moderated, rel=ugc)
@@index([game, status, hidden, players])
@@index([country, game])
@@index([provider, lastSeenAt])
```
Keep `connKey/ipKey` + `@@unique([source, sourceKey])`. Uniqueness across providers stays enforced at read time by the pure dedupe; add a **write-time** guard: before insert, if another row has the same `connKey`, merge (provider list array `providers String[]`) instead of creating a second row, so counts per source remain honest.

### 3.3 New tables
- `DirectorySource` (one row per provider): `key`, `enabled` (default false), `showPublic` (default false), `scheduleMinutes`, `lastRunAt`, `lastOkAt`, `lastError`, `consecutiveErrors`, `circuitOpenUntil`, `cursor`, `needsKey`, `termsReviewedBy`, `termsReviewedAt`, `termsUrl`, `attributionText`. The "terms reviewed" fields are a hard gate: provider cannot be enabled unless set (legal checkpoint made mechanical).
- `DirectoryProbeSample` (keep small): `serverId`, `at`, `alive`, `players`, `rttMs`; retain 14 days at 15-30-min grain for ALIVE rows only; roll up to `uptime7d` and a daily peak table `DirectoryDaily(serverId, day, peak, avg, uptimePct)` for 90 days. Only for servers shown or candidates for pages (not all 150k: sample the top ~10k).
- `DirectoryOptOut`: `kind` (ip | ip:port | hostname | cidr | connKey-hash), `value`, `reason`, `requestedBy` (email hash), `verifiedAt`, `createdAt`. Consulted by EVERY provider's upsert and by the prober (never probe an opted-out address).
- `DirectoryReport`: `serverId`, `reason` (spam|abuse|not-mine|offensive|wrong-info), `reporterIpHash`, `note`, `status`. Auto-hide at N distinct reporters pending review.
- `DirectorySubmission`: owner-submitted pending verification (`game`, `address`, `token`, `expiresAt`, `userId`, `attempts`).

### 3.4 Liveness and pruning
- Prober is separate from ingest: it takes rows by `lastProbeAt ASC` within tiers: shown/high-traffic every 15 min; the rest every 6 h; DEAD rows every 24 h then stop.
- State machine: ALIVE -> 2 consecutive failed probes = DEGRADED (shown with a "may be offline" tag? No: hide from pages, keep in admin) -> 6 failures / 24 h = DEAD (hidden everywhere) -> deleted after 7 days dead (3 days for Steam rows, as today) or if the source stops listing it. Rows from owner-submitted: stay 30 days dead before removal + email the owner.
- A row needs BOTH: source says present within TTL AND last probe alive within 24 h, to appear publicly. Steam-only rows with an unprobeable game get TTL 24 h and a "listed on Steam" label, never "online".
- Players/max shown with "updated N min ago" (already the rule). Never show a number older than 60 min as "live".
- Reject lies: `players > max`, `max > game cap`, probe name differs wildly from source name (hijacked listing), identical (name,players) across >20 IPs (spam farm).

### 3.5 Taxonomy (categories/tags)
- Per-game mode enums live in a new `lib/directory-taxonomy.ts` keyed by family, derived from `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` where possible (e.g. rust: vanilla/modded/softcore, wipe cycle, pvp/pve; minecraft: survival, skyblock, factions, minigames, creative, prison, towny, roleplay, modded, bedrock-crossplay, anarchy; gmod: darkrp, ttt, sandbox, prophunt, murder; valheim: pve, pvp, hardcore, modded, vanilla+; pz: vanilla, build-42, roleplay, hardcore).
- Mapping order: owner-set > source tags (`gametype`, MOTD keywords) via per-game keyword rules > unset. Always store the evidence; unknown stays null, never guess ("nothing is invented" rule from valve.ts).
- Global facets: country, region, passworded, modded, players band, language (only if owner-set), uptime band, "Hosted on Nxeon".

### 3.6 Abuse/spam, safety, privacy
- Display ONLY: name (sanitised), a public join address (ip:port or domain:port, already what the source publishes), game, mode, map, players/max, version, country. Never: A2S_PLAYER names, Steam IDs, admin contacts, RCON/query ports unless the join port equals them, hosting node IPs of Nxeon servers (existing rule), SLP player samples, owner email, internal IDs.
- Address hygiene: reject private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/multicast/our own ranges (extend the existing regex to include 100.64/10, 224/4, 240/4, IPv6 equivalents); resolve hostnames once, pin the resolved IP for the probe, reject if it resolves to private (SSRF) and re-check on each probe (DNS rebinding). Ports < 1024 and well-known service ports (22, 25, 53, 80, 443, 3306...) rejected (a "game server" at :22 is a port scan vector).
- Probe politeness: global pps cap, per-destination-IP cap (1/s, max 4 concurrent), per-/24 cap, jittered schedule, UA/identification in the TCP-level payload where the protocol allows, a public page `/directory/probe-info` explaining who we are and how to opt out (put abuse@ contact), honour opt-out within 24 h, run from a node-2 worker (blast radius away from the primary's IP reputation, which also sends email).
- Name moderation: strip control/RTL chars (existing), collapse markup/colour codes (Minecraft section sign, FiveM ^1, Unity rich text), run a word filter (slurs/porn/gambling) -> auto-hide + admin queue; never render HTML; images only after review.
- Spam controls for owner-submitted: Nxeon account + verified email required, 5 pending/ 20 total listings per account, probe token verification, cool-down, captcha on anonymous (if we allow anonymous - recommend NO).
- GDPR/privacy: a server IP of a home-hosted server can be personal data; basis = legitimate interest + easy opt-out; update privacy policy (also REQUIRED by the Steam terms: country of storage + what Steam data is stored); retention as above; no player-level data at all.
- Takedown/opt-out: public `/directory/remove` form: enter address -> we probe and show a token to put in the server name OR the owner emails from the domain's WHOIS/abuse contact OR logs in as the Nxeon owner. Verified requests insert `DirectoryOptOut` immediately (row hidden at once; permanent exclusion). Unverified urgent requests (abuse/safety/DMCA-like) -> admin can hide on trust with a 7-day verification window. SLA stated on the page: 72 h max, target 24 h.

### 3.7 Images policy
- Game covers: only Nxeon-owned art (as now; no Valve/Steam/publisher store art without a licence check). 
- Server pictures: customer-uploaded or owner-supplied URLs are NEVER rendered until admin approval (existing `mediaApproved` rule); re-approval on change; hotlinking third-party images disallowed - fetch, re-encode (strip EXIF), serve from our CDN after approval. Minecraft favicons: treat as owner picture (approval needed). Auto-NSFW screening optional later (cost: a classifier call; not before P4).
- External (Steam-sourced) rows get the game cover only.

## 4. INGEST ARCHITECTURE

### 4.1 Provider interface (mirrors `lib/modsync/types.ts`)
```ts
// lib/directory-ingest/types.ts
export interface DirectoryProvider {
  key: string;                     // "steam" | "vintagestory" | "owner" ...
  games: string[];                 // families it can serve
  policy: "list" | "verify-only";  // verify-only = only confirms addresses we already hold
  requiresEnv?: string[];          // STEAM_WEB_API_KEY -> status needs_key, parked 6 h (same as modsync)
  termsUrl: string;                // surfaced in admin
  attribution: { text: string; href: string; followLink: true };
  defaultIntervalMin: number;
  maxRequestsPerDay: number;       // enforced by the token bucket (Steam 100k/day cap, we use <2k)
  run(ctx: ProviderCtx, game: string): AsyncIterable<DirectoryCandidate[]>; // paged, resumable cursor
}
export type DirectoryCandidate = { provider; sourceKey; game; name; host; ip; port; queryPort; map; players; maxPlayers; version; tags; extra?: Json; connKey; ipKey };
```
- Existing `parseValveRow`/`ExternalCandidate` becomes the first provider (`steam`) with no behaviour change except the new fields; `scripts/directory-ingest.ts` stays as the manual CLI. Reuse `lib/modsync/http.ts` (move to `lib/net/polite-http.ts` or import as-is) for pacing/backoff/ETag/redaction (`redactUrl` for keys).
- Plug-in order in the upsert: sanitise -> geo -> opt-out check -> Nxeon-dedupe -> existing-key merge -> upsert (as run.ts does, but batching with `createMany`/raw upsert for 100k rows; today's per-row transaction of 100 is OK to ~50k rows per sweep: keep, measure).

### 4.2 Worker sweep
- `worker/directory.ts` ticks every 5 min like `modsyncTick()`; DB claim (`DirectorySource.runningUntil`) so two processes never overlap; one bounded slice (<= 5 min) per tick; cursor saved in `DirectorySource.cursor`.
- Cadence defaults: steam list per game every 60 min (Rust/CS2/GMod every 2-4 h: they are big and low value per refresh); owner-submitted: none (event driven); vintagestory: 6 h.
- Prober is a second tick (`directoryProbeTick`) with its own budget (max ~4 min, concurrency 200 UDP sockets, token bucket global 300 pps).
- Backoff: exponential 1 -> 2 -> 4 ... up to 6 h on errors, honour `Retry-After`/429; **circuit breaker**: 5 consecutive failures OR HTTP 401/403 => `circuitOpenUntil = now+6h`, status shown in admin; 403 from Steam = key revoked => auto-disable provider and alert.
- **Kill switches (all default OFF, in `Setting` and per-`DirectorySource`)**: `directory_ingest_enabled` (global ingest), per-provider `enabled`, `directory_external_show` (public display, global), per-provider `showPublic`, `directory_probe_enabled`, `directory_owner_submissions_enabled`. A provider can be shown but not ingested (and vice versa). Flipping `showPublic` off instantly hides that provider's rows from all pages and the sitemap (cached pages revalidate; also add on-demand `revalidateTag('directory')`).
- Safety rails: refuse to publish a sweep that shrinks the game's list by >60% vs the previous (likely an API outage/partial response: keep old rows, mark run as `suspicious`); min row count sanity; max rows per game per provider (e.g. 20k) with a "top by players/described" cap.

### 4.3 Observability (`/admin/directory` additions)
Per provider: enabled/show toggles, terms-reviewed stamp and link, last run, last OK, next run, duration, rows fetched/inserted/updated/deduped/pruned/rejected (by reason: private ip, bad name, optout, dup), circuit state, error stream (last 20, keys redacted), requests today vs budget (Steam 100k cap bar). Per game: live count (ALIVE), shown count, indexable-page status and why/why-not, geo coverage, probe success rate. Prober: pps, queue age, fail rate by probe kind. Reports queue, opt-out list, submissions queue, approve/hide/feature, bulk "hide provider X". Alerts via existing fleet-alerts: provider dead >24 h, rows shrink >60%, probe success <50%.

### 4.4 Cost / load (estimates, UNVERIFIED sizes: confirm with ONE owner-approved sample call per game)
- Rows steady state: Steam-listed families maybe 60k-150k total (Rust/CS2/CS16/GMod dominate; many are junk and dropped by dedupe/spam rules). Owner-submitted: hundreds to low thousands in year 1. Minecraft: only what owners submit/verify.
- Row size ~0.4 KB incl. indexes => 150k rows ~ 60-100 MB. Probe samples: keep for top 10k shown rows x 96/day x 14 d x ~40 B = ~540 MB worst case; trim to 30-min grain => ~270 MB; use rollups to bound. Annual growth under 1 GB.
- Requests: Steam list sweeps ~35 games x 24/day = ~840 API calls/day (limit 100k). Probes: tier1 10k rows x 96 = ~1M/day? too many; tier1 only for ~3k most visible rows (every 15 min = 288k/day), tier2 120k rows x 4 = ~480k/day. Total ~0.8M UDP/TCP exchanges/day ~ 10 pps average; bandwidth <0.2 GB/day. CPU trivial in a node-2 worker. DB writes: 0.8M samples/day if every probe wrote a row; instead write only state CHANGES + rollups (~50k writes/day).
- Money: $0 external (Steam key is free). Human costs: moderation queue, abuse mail.

## 5. INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE and UX

### 5.1 Marketing site (public, SEO)
URL tree (all under existing `/game-servers/directory`, minecraft stays `/servers`, link the two):
```
/game-servers/directory                      HUB
/game-servers/directory/<game>               GAME page
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<country>     COUNTRY page   (e.g. /rust/germany)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<mode>        MODE page      (e.g. /rust/pvp-vanilla, /minecraft/skyblock)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/best          "Best <game> servers" curated (monthly refresh, human-reviewed intro)
/game-servers/directory/<game>/<country>/<mode>  only if >= thresholds (rare)
/game-servers/directory/s/<slug>             SERVER page  (ONLY Nxeon-hosted or owner-claimed+verified+described)
/directory/remove  /directory/add  /directory/probe-info   utility pages (noindex except probe-info)
```
Wireframes:
- **Hub**: hero ("Find a public server for <N> games" with live total only when real), search box (game or server name), game cover grid sorted by live players (cover tile = existing component), "Featured on Nxeon" shelf (<=6, rules below), region tabs, footer with Valve/other attributions and the "how listing works / remove your server" links, CTA band "Host your own - from $X/mo" and "List your server (free)".
- **Game page**: breadcrumb; H1 "<Game> public servers (live)"; stat strip (servers online, players now, countries) with "updated N min ago"; filter bar (country, mode, players band, passworded, modded, "Hosted on Nxeon"); list (20/page, server-rendered, paginated with `rel=next/prev` not infinite-scroll) rows = [cover or game glyph] name, address copy button, mode chip, country flag, players/max bar, ping-from-region, last seen; right rail: "Run a server like these" CTA tied to the game's hosting page + game's mod/pack links; below fold: 150-300 words of unique, human-written guide (how to join, popular modes, how Nxeon verifies) + FAQ. Aggregate stats per country as a small table (internal linking).
- **Country/mode page**: same template, H1 "<Mode> <Game> servers in <Country>", unique stat sentence generated from data (counts, busiest hours from our history - real), top 10, and links to sibling countries/modes.
- **Server page** (only when it passes the gate): name, owner description (moderated), join instructions per game (copy-paste), live status, 7-day uptime/peak chart (from our samples), screenshots (approved), "Hosted on Nxeon" badge + "Host your own like this" CTA, nearby/similar servers, report/claim buttons. Reason for gating: thin/duplicate content risk; individual pages for 100k stranger servers = doorway pages.
- **Indexing policy (extends INDEX_MIN_DESCRIBED)**: index only if ALL: >= 5 servers ALIVE in last 24 h (probe verified) for the page's facet; >= 3 with owner description or >= 10 with distinct non-templated names; unique intro text present; data fresh (<24 h); no more than 50% of rows from one IP/ASN/hoster (anti-spam-farm). Else `noindex,follow` and omitted from the sitemap, but still crawlable by users (links keep working). Paginated pages 2+ are `noindex,follow`; canonical to page 1 (query-param filters canonicalise to the clean URL). Server pages: index only Nxeon-hosted/claimed with description >=60 chars + 7-day uptime >=80%; all others have no page (modal on list). Sitemap `lastmod` = last meaningful change, not every refresh. Nothing programmatic should create pages for combos with <thresholds (prevents the 100k thin-page trap).
- Structured data: `BreadcrumbList` everywhere; `ItemList` (+ `ListItem` name/url) on list pages; `FAQPage` only on pages with visible FAQ content; `Organization` already global. There is NO schema.org type for a game server listing: do NOT fake `Product`/`Review`/`AggregateRating`/`VideoGame` per server (policy-risky). `WebPage` + `dateModified` is fine.
- Other: `rel="ugc nofollow noopener"` on owner links (existing); Valve attribution link followed (`rel="noopener"` only) per Steam terms; no outbound links to a hoster unless owner-approved; hreflang not needed for v2.0 (English only; country pages are targeted content, not translations).
- Avoiding duplicate/thin content: unique intro per game and per big country (humans + Claude drafts, human-reviewed), real computed stats, canonical rules above, no "x servers in <city>" templated pages (country max), consistent H1/title schema ("Best Rust servers 2026 - live list | Nxeon" only when the page really is refreshed monthly; no fake year bumps).

### 5.2 Customer portal
- `/dashboard/servers/browse` (name TBD, inside the existing portal shell): tabs [Browse | Favourites | My listings]. Left filters: game (multi), country/region, mode, players (min/max or "has players", "not full"), ping-from-your-region (we know the viewer's country via geo-ip; nearest probe region), passworded, modded, "Nxeon-hosted", sort (players, recently verified, uptime, newest). Result card same as marketing row + [Favourite star] [Copy address] [Join help]. Empty-state: "No servers yet for <game>/<filter>: Host the first one".

- **Steam master list is the only large legitimate source, and it's amber.** I read the Steam Web API terms, and the clauses that matter are:
  - Valve name, logo and links are required on any page showing Steam data, and the Valve link may not be `nofollow`.
  - The data may not appear endorsed by Valve or "available from a third party".
  - The storage country must be named in the privacy policy.
  - There is a 100,000 calls/day cap, and Valve can revoke access without notice.
  - Honest read: the terms are written around an "Application" and end users, so using them for a public SEO directory is an interpretation, not an explicit grant.
- **Direct probes are our own data.** Direct A2S, Minecraft Java status and Bedrock RakNet queries are green, but only for addresses we learned from permitted sources. I recommend never scanning address space, and never storing player names.
- **Owner-submitted servers are the answer for games with no list.** The owner proves control by putting a one-time token in the server name or MOTD, and the prober reads it back. This works for Minecraft, which has no official list, and for every other game without a source.
- **Aggregators and HTML scraping are red.** I recommend not ingesting BattleMetrics (the 60 req/min anonymous and 300/min token figures come from search snippets of its API docs, which our fetcher couldn't open) or Minecraft/other listing sites.   - factorio: its API needs a personal username and token
  - fivem: the list endpoint is undocumented
  - eco and enshrouded: unverified, so they stay here until checked
- **Rough load.** About 60–150k rows, about 0.8M probes a day (roughly 10 per second), under 1 GB a year, and no external cost.

- A per-family source matrix for all 48 distinct family keys. The schema file lists `projectzomboid` twice, which is why the brief says 49.
- Additive changes to `ExternalServer`, plus new tables for provider config, probe history, opt-outs, reports and submissions.
- A `DirectoryProvider` interface mirroring the mod providers, with a worker sweep, circuit breakers and kill switches that default off.
- Marketing and portal information architecture with wireframe-level descriptions and indexing thresholds.
- A phased build: P1 to P4 is about 16–21 agent-days. P1 turns on the existing Valve ingest with attribution, a schedule and a liveness prober.
- Legal checkpoints per source and 8 owner decisions.

**What I could not verify, all marked UNVERIFIED in the plan**
- Steam app IDs beyond the 11 already in code, and list sizes, are from memory. One approved sample call per game would settle them.
- The terms for Factorio, FiveM/Cfx.re, Vintage Story, TruckersMP and Eco were not read.
- The Minecraft Usage Guidelines wording comes from secondary summaries, so the owner should reread the primary page.
- Whether Valheim crossplay, Enshrouded, V Rising and Palworld servers appear on the Steam list is unknown.
- The legal ratings are engineering judgement, not legal advice.
